question: What is the main focus of community-centred nursing care?

options.A: Promoting health within people's living environments
options.B: Conducting laboratory tests for rare diseases
options.D: Treating severe illnesses inside hospital wards

explanation: Community-centred care focuses on meeting people in their homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces to promote health rather than waiting for them to arrive at a hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is community-centred care considered a shift from traditional hospital nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any medications or clinical equipment
options.B: It focuses only on newborn babies and ignores elderly populations
options.C: It moves the focus from treating sickness in facilities to preventing illness in neighborhoods
options.D: It relies entirely on doctors rather than nurses to provide care

explanation: Traditional nursing often waits for patients to become sick enough to enter a hospital, whereas community-centred care proactively addresses health where people live. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: What does equity mean in the context of primary health care?

options.A: Only wealthy individuals pay for health services
options.B: Essential health services are accessible to everyone
options.C: Doctors earn the same salary as community health workers
options.D: Every clinic has the exact same amount of money

explanation: Equity ensures fair distribution of health services so that all members of the community can access the care they need, regardless of financial standing. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration important in primary health care?

options.A: It allows doctors to control local government policies
options.B: It ensures that hospitals make a higher financial profit
options.C: Health is influenced by factors like food, education, and housing, not just medicine
options.D: It stops nurses from having to do any home visits

explanation: Because health depends on social determinants like clean water, education, and nutrition, health sectors must work alongside agriculture, education, and public works. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which service is a key part of disease prevention in comprehensive health care?
explanation: Immunizations stop preventable infectious diseases from spreading through a community, making them a core preventive service. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: A community nurse helps a stroke patient practice daily walking exercises to regain strength. Which component of comprehensive care does this represent?
explanation: Helping a patient recover lost functions and achieve independence after an illness or injury falls directly under rehabilitative care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a windshield survey in community nursing?

options.B: Testing the vision of drivers in local transport parks
options.C: Observing a neighborhood by walking or driving through it
options.D: Reviewing hospital financial statements in an office

explanation: A windshield survey is a quick observational method where the nurse assesses community housing, sanitation, and general environment firsthand. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is it important to talk directly with community residents during a health assessment rather than just reading clinic records?

options.A: Government rules forbid nurses from reading clinic data
options.B: Clinic records miss people who cannot or do not visit the health facility
options.C: Community members prefer filling out paper forms to seeing nurses
options.D: Patients always lie to doctors when they are inside a clinic

explanation: Clinic records only show individuals who manage to seek care, leaving out vulnerable people who lack access or transport. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: What does cultural competence require a nurse to do?

options.A: Speak at least five foreign languages fluently
options.B: Insist that patients abandon their cultural heritage
options.C: Adopt every traditional lifestyle practice personally
options.D: Respect and work effectively with local cultural beliefs

explanation: Cultural competence requires understanding and respecting patient beliefs to provide safe and acceptable care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the best reaction when a community nurse discovers a patient is using traditional herbal remedies alongside prescribed drugs?

options.A: Refuse to treat the patient until they sign an apology
options.B: Yell at the patient immediately and throw the herbs away
options.C: Report the patient to local security agencies at once
options.D: Discuss the herbs calmly to check for any dangerous drug interactions

explanation: A non-judgmental approach helps patients feel safe to share their habits, allowing the nurse to protect them from harmful drug-herb interactions. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What does sustainability mean for a community health program?

options.A: The community can maintain the program after external funding ends
options.B: The program receives unlimited money from the government forever
options.C: Foreign experts run the project without stopping
options.D: No evaluation is ever required after setup

explanation: A sustainable program is built to last using local capacity and resources so it does not collapse when outside donors depart. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure a health project is sustainable?

options.A: Involving village leaders in planning from the very beginning
options.B: Relying entirely on foreign staff to make every daily decision
options.C: Using affordable materials available within the local market
options.D: Training local residents as community health volunteers

explanation: Depending completely on outside staff creates dependency and guarantees the project will fail once those outsiders leave. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)
